name: close-confirmation
whatItDemonstrates: A tweet-composer dialog whose close requests are intercepted when the textarea has text, opening a nested AlertDialog confirmation instead of closing.
stateManaged: controlled — three useState values: dialogOpen, confirmationOpen, and textareaValue; the parent Root's onOpenChange shows the confirmation instead of closing when text is present, otherwise closes normally and resets the textarea
nonTrivialInteractions: onOpenChange intercepts close requests (backdrop click, Esc, Cancel button) when textareaValue is non-empty and opens the confirmation dialog instead of closing
form submit closes the dialog via setDialogOpen(false)
confirmation's Discard button closes both dialogs (setConfirmationOpen(false) then setDialogOpen(false)); Go back (AlertDialog.Close) only dismisses the confirmation
titleId from React.useId is set on Dialog.Title and referenced by the textarea's aria-labelledby since there is no Dialog.Description
popup styling reads var(--nested-dialogs) for offset/scale and uses data-nested-dialog-open with a ::after overlay to dim the parent behind the confirmation dialog

name: detached-triggers-controlled
whatItDemonstrates: Three detached triggers sharing one typed handle (each with a distinct numeric payload) drive a fully controlled dialog, alongside a plain button that opens it programmatically targeting a specific trigger.
stateManaged: controlled — useState for open and triggerId; handleOpenChange syncs both, deriving triggerId from eventDetails.trigger?.id; the programmatic button sets triggerId('trigger-2') and open(true) directly
nonTrivialInteractions: Dialog.createHandle<number>() created at module scope and passed to three detached Triggers and the Root
Root uses the function-as-a-child pattern ({ payload }) => ... to render the conditional 'Dialog {payload}' title from the opening trigger's payload
onOpenChange's eventDetails.trigger?.id keeps triggerId in sync so ARIA trigger state stays correct when the dialog is closed via Dialog.Close or backdrop
programmatic open without a trigger click uses triggerId='trigger-2' to associate the open state with that trigger

name: detached-triggers-simple
whatItDemonstrates: The minimal detached-trigger setup: a Trigger rendered outside Dialog.Root, linked to it purely through a shared createHandle() handle.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — no open-state props; the handle-linked trigger toggles Root's internal open state
nonTrivialInteractions: Dialog.createHandle() at module scope shared by the detached Trigger and the Root
Root contains no Trigger child; all its content is Portal/Popup markup

name: focus-management
whatItDemonstrates: A feedback-form dialog where initialFocus moves focus to the feedback input on open and finalFocus returns focus to a button outside the dialog on close.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — no open-state props; only two refs (initialFocusRef, finalFocusRef) used as focus targets
nonTrivialInteractions: initialFocus and finalFocus are set to refs passed to Dialog.Popup
initialFocusRef is attached to the second Field.Control (the feedback input) so it receives focus on open
finalFocusRef is attached to a plain button rendered outside the Dialog.Root entirely, demonstrating focusing an element outside the dialog on close

name: hero
whatItDemonstrates: A basic centered modal dialog — trigger, dimming backdrop, title and description, and a close button — with open/close transitions.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — no open-state props; Root manages open state internally via Trigger and Close
nonTrivialInteractions: enter/exit transitions driven by data-starting-style and data-ending-style classes on Backdrop (opacity) and Popup (scale + opacity)

name: inside-scroll
whatItDemonstrates: A scrollable dialog that stays fully on screen: Dialog.Viewport acts as a fixed positioning container while an inner Scroll Area scrolls the long popup content.
stateManaged: none — uncontrolled dialog with static CONTENT_SECTIONS data rendered as sections
nonTrivialInteractions: Dialog.Viewport is used as a fixed flex centering container (not a scroller) with overflow-hidden
ScrollArea.Root/Viewport inside the Popup scrolls the content (min-h-0/flex-auto so it shrinks within max-h-full popup)
custom scrollbar visibility toggled by data-hovering/data-scrolling states

name: nested
whatItDemonstrates: A second dialog nested inside the first: a 'Customize' button in the parent popup opens a child dialog on top while the parent stays visible behind it.
stateManaged: none — two independent uncontrolled Dialog.Roots, each toggled by its own Trigger
nonTrivialInteractions: inner Dialog.Root (with its own Trigger/Portal/Popup) is rendered inside the outer popup
both popups style themselves from var(--nested-dialogs) (top offset and scale) and use data-nested-dialog-open with a ::after overlay to dim the dialog underneath
only the outermost Portal renders a Backdrop; the nested Portal has none so the parent shows through cleanly

name: open-from-menu
whatItDemonstrates: A menu item ('Details…') opens a controlled dialog imperatively through its onClick handler; the dialog has no Trigger of its own.
stateManaged: controlled — useState dialogOpen; Menu.Item's onClick sets it true and Dialog.Root's onOpenChange={setDialogOpen} keeps it in sync
nonTrivialInteractions: Menu.Item onClick={() => setDialogOpen(true)} opens the dialog after the menu closes
Dialog.Root rendered with no Trigger inside or outside it — opened only via external state
Menu.Portal/Positioner/Popup with sideOffset=8 and align=start position the menu

name: outside-scroll
whatItDemonstrates: An outer Scroll Area inside Dialog.Viewport scrolls the page-like container so the popup can extend past the bottom edge, with a slide-up/slide-down transition.
stateManaged: none — uncontrolled dialog; only a popupRef used as its own initialFocus target
nonTrivialInteractions: ScrollArea.Root/Viewport wrap the popup inside Dialog.Viewport; ScrollArea.Content uses min-h-full centering and popup margins (my-16) let it overflow and extend past the bottom edge
ScrollArea.Root overrides its default positioning with style={{ position: undefined }} so it fills the Viewport
initialFocus={popupRef} points focus at the popup itself so opening doesn't focus the first link

slide-in/out transitions via data-starting-style/data-ending-style translate-y, with motion-reduce:transition-none and group data-ending-style on the Viewport disabling pointer events and hiding the scrollbar during close
icon-only Dialog.Close exposes an aria-label

name: uncontained
whatItDemonstrates: A popup with no visible container of its own: the Popup is a transparent pointer-events-none positioning layer whose children (the colored surface and a floating close button) opt back into pointer events.
stateManaged: none — uncontrolled dialog with no state props
nonTrivialInteractions: Dialog.Popup gets pointer-events: none while the inner colored surface div and the absolutely positioned Dialog.Close get pointer-events: auto so backdrop clicks still register
Close button sits visually outside the colored popup area but remains inside the Popup to stay in the tab order and be announced correctly
decorative scale-in transition on the surface via group/popup data-starting-style
no Title/Description parts are used in this layout demo
